matches.rationale: GT 1 concerns inconsistency between the table in Figure 6(b) and the learning curves in Figure 6(a). No finding addresses this figure-table cross-check; Pred 4 identifies a different inconsistency (Figure 6(b) vs. Appendix Table 2), not the claim that tabulated metrics are inflated relative to the plotted curves.

GT 2 identifies a sign error in the definition of f^{return} where a minus sign makes maximizing the objective discourage good actions. Pred 1 identifies exactly this issue, noting the minus sign before Â^{ref} causes a sign reversal and the correct form should use +Â^{ref}.

GT 3 concerns undisclosed hyperparameter values (p) in the main paper and selective reporting that obscures sensitivity to tuning. No finding mentions this omission or the hyperparameter disclosure issue.

GT 4 is about overstated claims in the abstract ('eliminates sample inefficiency', 'completely solves training instability'). No finding addresses rhetorical overstatement in the abstract or unsupported claims of elimination/solving.

GT 5 flags potentially fabricated citations 'Deng et al., 2025' and 'Cheng et al., 2025' in the Related Work section. Pred 3 identifies a different fabricated/missing citation ('Kumar et al. [2024]' in the Introduction). These are distinct citations in different sections and thus different scientific issues.
GT 6 concerns the absence of ethical discussion, failure modes, and societal impact for RLHF toxicity mitigation. No finding identifies this ethical omission.

GT 7 identifies marketing-style rhetorical exaggeration in the Introduction ('completely solves', 'unprecedented', 'revolutionary breakthrough'). No finding addresses promotional tone or rhetorical manipulation in the Introduction.

GT 8 identifies a contradiction between Section 3.1 (π^{ref} = π_{θ^{(k)}}, dynamic per-round) and Appendix A.2 (fixed reference policy). Pred 2 captures precisely this contradiction, noting the text describes the reference as both 'fixed, pre-trained' and 'dynamic, evolving with training.'
GT 9 concerns manipulated y-axis ranges in Figure 6(a) that visually exaggerate differences. No finding addresses visual encoding manipulation or axis-range cropping.

GT 10 identifies an unfair experimental design where IIF benefits from environment-specific hyperparameter tuning while baselines use defaults. No finding addresses this asymmetry in experimental protocol.

GT 11 flags wide confidence intervals and overclaimed consistency ('consistently improves' vs. evidence of performance degradation). No finding addresses statistical power, confidence interval width, or cherry-picked interpretations of consistency.
GT 12 concerns the missing learning rate η_j in the influence score formula and notational inconsistency about θ_j^{(k)}. No finding identifies this missing component or notational ambiguity.
GT 13 concerns selective environment reporting where failure cases are hidden. No finding addresses undisclosed negative results or cherry-picked success environments.

GT 14 identifies misattribution of the f^{return} formulation to standard REINFORCE-with-baseline from Sutton & Barto, when the formulation is a novel construction. Pred 1 identifies a sign error in the same passage but does not flag the incorrect citation or conceptual conflation of the formulation with established theory.

GT 15 identifies a contradiction between the main text's claim of 'negligible overhead' and Appendix B.9 data showing influence calculation is 7-15% of per-round time. No finding addresses this computational cost contradiction.
